newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian oil pipeline burst triggers huge fire.
newsitem.headline: Indian oil pipeline burst triggers huge fire.

text.p: A massive fire broke out after an oil pipeline belonging to India's state-run Oil India Ltd (OIL) burst early on Thursday in the northeastern state of Assam, company officials said.
The burst forced the closure of two major refineries, an OIL official said.
There was a large crude oil spill when the pipeline burst at Chaulkhoa near Nalbari, about 55 km (34 miles) north of the state capital of Guwahati, they told Reuters by telephone.
An engineer manning the company's control room said the oil spill caught fire soon afterwards, but he was unable to say what caused the fire.
"There was a leak in the pipeline and the oil spill caught fire," said an engineer who declined to be identified. "The fire has been brought under control."
There were no immediate reports of casualties.
"The fire could be seen from about a kilometre," UNI said, adding that fire tenders had been sent in to control the blaze.
"We have not received any further information," the OIL engineer said. "Officials are at the site."
Earlier the United News of India (UNI) news agency reported the pipeline exploded, triggering a massive fire.
